# LightRAG patent evidence provenance
Source-field ablation and chunk-boundary control

**Result:** the source fields let the model identify the correct patent but are not enough to recover the claim numbers; with the claim text added, the core question is answered correctly, but the citation numbers are still wrong. In the manual chunking control, the complete technical relation is kept 3/3 under the same-chunk condition and 0/3 under the cross-chunk condition; local facts still exist. The explicit “another patent” error of the original Q11 did not recur in the 3 replays of A.

This round only reuses the saved Q11 context and the original text of the same patent; there was no new retrieval and the 20-document index was not rebuilt. The results apply to this model, this prompt and these control conditions; they allow no inference about error rates in natural corpora and cannot be attributed to the original implementation of the 2025 paper.

## 2. Source-field ablation: Q11's retrieval result frozen

The API 392 request of round two's supplementary Q11 mix is frozen: 82 entities, 82 relations, 20 original text chunks, a 13-entry Reference List. A replays its system/user text and generation parameters exactly. 3 runs per condition, in the orders ABC / BCA / CAB; output cap 3500 in all.

| Condition | The only new content | What is kept |
| ---|---|--- |
| A original | none; original context | Original entities, relation descriptions, order, original text chunks, user question, instructions and reference list all unchanged. Retrieval is not rerun. |
| B source-enhanced | publication_numbers, file_path and source_id added to all 82 existing relations. |  |
| C sources + text | B plus the complete original text of claims 1 and 27 of US7991757B2; this is an additional evidence diagnostic. |  |

Every source_id was traced back to the stored chunk, full_doc_id, file_path and character span in the original document. `&lt;SEP&gt;` joins aggregated sources; it cannot be inferred that each sentence corresponds one-to-one to a claim. B adds a combination of three fields; the contribution of any single field cannot be separated, and adding fields also changes the context length.

Key existing relation: `External Recommender → Registration Module`; `file_path=US7991757B2.txt`; `source_id=US7991757B2-chunk-000&lt;SEP&gt;US7991757B2-chunk-001`. B adds no claim text or claim-number evidence.

| Measure (3 runs per condition) | A | B | C |
| ---|---|---|--- |
| Affirmative wrong source attribution/exclusion in the text | 0/3 | 0/3 | 0/3 |
| Identifies the US7991757B2 source correctly | 0/3 | 3/3 | 3/3 |
| Core claim task completed with supporting evidence | 0/3 | 0/3 | 3/3 |
| Trailing References provide no evidence of the target patent | 3/3 | 3/3 | 0/3 |
| Target patent source and citation number both right | 0/3 | 0/3 | 0/3 |
| Citation numbers conflict with the original mapping | 0/3 | 0/3 | 3/3 |

**Interpretation:** all three A runs say that a visible source mapping is missing and refuse to attribute the graph descriptions to the target patent; all three B runs identify the document source but rightly refuse to guess claims 1/27; all three C runs answer the difference between the claims and the explicit dependency correctly. It cannot be claimed that B stably fixes the affirmative “different patent family” error of the original API 392, because that error did not recur in A. A and B both append trailing References of other patents that do not support the target registration capabilities; since there are no sentence-level citations, the text cannot be forcibly matched to individual entries.

**Citation limitation:** to keep the ablation pure, the Reference List of all three conditions does not add US799; the original [1] is still US10867122B1. Yet C outputs `[1] US7991757B2.txt` all three times, i.e. the source document is right but the number mapping conflicts. This part of the failure is limited by the control design keeping the old reference list and cannot be stated as “the official end-to-end citation of a normally added document necessarily fails”. A production system needs to keep evidence sources and citation IDs in sync.

**Verbatim quotes:** C's core claim conclusion being correct does not mean that everything in quotation marks is verbatim. All three normalise punctuation; C1 writes the original `being provided` as `are provided` and adds a mechanism explanation that is explicitly marked as an inference but not directly supported by the text. The report therefore counts content, verbatimness and citation mapping separately.

C1: complete actual answer

```
**US7991757B2 — Registration Capabilities in Claims 1 and 27**

**Claim 1 (explicit evidence).** Claim 1 recites a system comprising a "registration module configured to provide functionality for registering an external recommender with a recommendations service." The same claim also requires a "data interface operative to provide access to the event data to a plurality of external recommenders registered with the recommendations service," where those recommenders "are provided by one or more entities that differ from a provider of the recommendations service." So Claim 1's registration capability is the basic function of registering an external recommender with the service.

**Claim 27 (explicit evidence).** Claim 27 depends from Claim 1 ("The system of claim 1") and adds a further configuration of the same module: "wherein the registration module is further configured to allow a provider of an external recommender associated with the plurality of external recommenders to provide machine readable descriptions of the external recommender."

**Dependency and relationship.** The dependency is stated expressly in Claim 27's opening phrase, "The system of claim 1." Because Claim 27 incorporates Claim 1, its added capability is a narrowing limitation on the registration module already recited in Claim 1 — namely, enabling the recommender's provider to supply machine-readable descriptions of that recommender.

**Inference (not explicit).** It can reasonably be inferred that Claim 27's machine-readable descriptions are the mechanism by which an external recommender is registered and made accessible via Claim 1's data interface; however, the claims do not expressly state that link, so this is inference rather than quoted fact.

```

**US7991757B2 — Registration Capability in Claims 1 and 27**

**Claim 1 (explicit evidence).** Claim 1 recites a system comprising a "registration module configured to provide functionality for registering an external recommender with a recommendations service." The same claim also requires a "data interface operative to provide access to the event data to a plurality of external recommenders registered with the recommendations service," where those recommenders are "provided by one or more entities that differ from a provider of the recommendations service." So Claim 1's registration capability is the module-level function of registering an external recommender with the service.

**Dependency and added capability.** The dependency is express — Claim 27 incorporates all limitations of Claim 1 and narrows the registration module. ## 3. Manual chunk-boundary control

The consecutive claims 26–28 from the original claims field of US7991757B2 are used, character span `[9973,10459)`, 486 characters, 93 o200k_base tokens. No original text is added, reordered or rewritten. Both conditions use 2 chunks without overlap and independent stateless extraction, with the same prompt and parameters, output cap 8192, gleaning=0. 3 runs per condition; orders SAME/CROSS, CROSS/SAME, SAME/CROSS.

| Condition | Boundary | Tokens per chunk | Target relation |
| ---|---|---|--- |
| SAME | Between claims 27 and 28, character 10329 of the original claims | 64 + 29 | The claim 27 sentence stays complete in the first chunk |
| CROSS | Inside claim 27, character 10270 of the original claims; before “ machine readable descriptions” | 55 + 38 | The first chunk ends with “to provide”, the second starts with the object |

The total API input tokens of the two calls per group are SAME 3721 and CROSS 3722; the original text has the same total, and the prompt wrapping and tokenization at the boundary cause a 1-token difference. The length and semantic completeness of each chunk change with the boundary and cannot be removed independently.

```
26. The system of claim 1 , wherein the computer system comprises multiple physical computing devices. 27. The system of claim 1 , wherein the registration module is further configured to allow a provider of an external recommender associated with the plurality of external recommenders to provide machine readable descriptions of the external recommender. 28. The system of claim 3 , wherein the content site selects at least some of the weights to assign to the external recommenders.
```

| Paired repeat | SAME complete relation | CROSS complete relation | Direct Module–Descriptions edge | Output truncation |
| ---|---|---|---|--- |
| 1 | kept | not kept | None in either condition; SAME expresses it as a Module–Provider relation description | none |
| 2 | kept | not kept | None in either condition; SAME expresses it as a Module–Provider relation description | none |
| 3 | kept | not kept | None in either condition; SAME expresses it as a Module–Provider relation description | none |

**Criterion:** the main measure accepts any officially parsed relation that faithfully expresses “the registration module allows a provider to supply machine readable descriptions of that recommender”; fixed entity endpoints are not required. The direct Module–Descriptions edge is 0/3 in both conditions; matching endpoint strings only would misjudge SAME's success as a failure.

SAME's actual relation descriptions include: “The registration module is configured to allow a provider of an external recommender to provide machine readable descriptions.” CROSS's corresponding description is only: “The registration module is configured to allow a provider of an external recommender to provide something.” The difference is already in the raw responses, and the official parser keeps each result, so in this control the complete relation is lost at the local extraction stage, not at parsing, graph indexing or retrieval.

**Limits:** CROSS still keeps part of the nodes/relation fragments of the module, the provider, the external recommender and the machine-readable descriptions; it cannot be said that all facts disappear. No joint cross-chunk re-extraction, graph-merge recovery or final QA was run, so it cannot be asserted that downstream steps necessarily cannot recover. The explicit legal dependency edge claim 27 → claim 1 is not materialised in either condition, and the default ontology does not require claim entities; this is not the main technical-relation measure of this control.

This is a manual stress test on a short 93-token snippet with zero overlap and a mid-sentence cut. It differs from round two's natural 1200-token/100-overlap chunking; in round two the technical relation of the original claims 1/27 across chunks was kept successfully. This round can support “a particular manual boundary makes independent extraction miss the complete relation”; it cannot give a frequency for natural chunking or claim a defect of the paper's original method.

## 4. Attribution and next research steps

| Observation | Supported attribution | Cannot be concluded |
| ---|---|--- |
| B restores the document source | With the retrieval result frozen, passing the existing relation sources into the answer context can improve the document attribution in this case. | The individual contributions of the three fields cannot be separated; it cannot be claimed that the original affirmative error is stably fixed. |
| C completes the core claim question | The original claim evidence supplies the numbers, the dependency and the original wording. | The improvement cannot be credited entirely to the source fields; it cannot be claimed that verbatim quotes and citation IDs are reliable. |
| C's citation [1] conflicts | Answer generation did not keep the mapping of the frozen reference list; the control design itself lacks a valid ID for the added document. | Cannot be taken as an unconditional failure rate of normal official end-to-end added evidence. |
| CROSS does not keep the complete technical relation | With the same text and number of calls, a manual mid-sentence boundary changes the evidence visible to local extraction. | Cannot be taken as all facts lost, a failure rate of natural chunks, or downstream non-recoverability. |

Valuable directions: refine the aggregated source_id into verifiable claim/character-span support; keep graph descriptions, original evidence and citation IDs in sync between retrieval and generation; recover cross-chunk evidence chains instead of relying on entity-name matching alone; evaluate with strict separation of document attribution, claim location, verbatim quotation and citation mapping, to identify where errors really occur.

## 5. Reproduction and verification scope

**Limitation of parser execution:** when the official operate module was imported normally, reading unrelated NumPy/PyYAML/NetworkX files on this machine stalled for a long time; those processes were stopped. No dependency or official source was modified or reinstalled. The substitute path compiles and executes directly the unmodified AST functions, helper functions and constants of the original source, records source spans and hashes, and uses the standard logger of the same name. For round two's normally parsed API 191, the totals of 42/34 node/edge groups, the 13 saved node groups and 4 edge groups (5 records) were checked to be identical, and the truncated edge is missing in the same way. The other records of round two were not saved and cannot be compared item by item, so equivalence for all possible inputs is not claimed.

The evidence package keeps the complete A/B/C requests, field-level diffs, a check of each of the 82 relations by source_id, claim character spans, the 21 actual requests with the complete provider JSON responses, the usage ledger, the two boundaries and their token spans, the officially parsed nodes/edges, the scoring script and the report. Round two's raw records are not overwritten; index hashes are checked before and after. All checks are AI-assisted evidence reviews and program assertions; no independent human annotation or statistical significance is claimed.

The A/B/C criteria were written into condition_manifest at 16:08:44, before the calls. The combined evaluation_protocol file was written at 16:12:40, 3 seconds after the 9 calls ended and before the main executor read the answers; this later file is not passed off as a pre-registration. The target wording for chunking was corrected to the original “external recommender” before the first chunking call; the criteria were not adjusted based on the chunking results. Temperature 0 and caching do not amount to independent random repeats.

## A. Completion, configuration and cost

This round reuses all data and the official source obtained in round one; no patents were downloaded again and no new model was deployed. Completion and embedding were first called separately: they returned OK and a valid 1×1024 vector; then a 2-document smoke index reached processed, giving 71 nodes / 90 edges, and real naive/mix QA was completed. The official query gate was met by **14:26:12 UTC** at the latest, before 15:13:44. The 20-document baseline ran from 14:27:54 to 14:42:21 UTC; all API calls fall within 14:21:39–14:52:26 UTC.

Round one stopped early at 13:45:45 UTC because there was no model service; its raw records and local report are kept intact, and this round does not overwrite that evidence. This round read the service settings temporarily from a secure configuration file specified by the user; the key was not written into the report, code, logs or a persistent environment. AutoDL was never accessed, and FOT, existing processes, weights, SSH tunnels and proxies were not touched.

| ---|--- |

The installed distribution metadata still says 1.5.8 from round one, but the runtime import path points explicitly to v1.5.7; the two versions are not conflated. |
| Data | [Dis2Pat](https://huggingface.co/datasets/lj408/Dis2Pat), 20 deduplicated English publication numbers on information retrieval/recommendation/contextual ranking/data indexing, 438 numbered claims. Full title, abstract and claims are written separately; file_paths is <publication number>.txt. The specification is only kept raw; the generated disclosure is not indexed. |

US8509827B2 claims 2/3 lack parent claim numbers in the original source; the formulas of US9218390B2 claims 10/11 are garbled. Nothing was filled in; the main questions avoid this content; the truncation case below lies in claim 2, which the garbling does not affect. |

The request and the returned model alias are recorded; the provider's announcement says the alias points to version 1017, but the service's internal build was not verified independently. |

JSON KV, NanoVectorDB, NetworkX; 20 processed, 0 failed; 612 nodes, 994 edges, no dangling source chunk IDs. |
| Extraction and generation | Official default extraction prompt; additional gleaning=0 (the source default is 1; a limitation of this run). temperature=0, maximum output 3500 tokens, thinking=false; SDK automatic retries=0, global call concurrency=2. 1 output truncation occurred and is not treated as lossless extraction. |
| Baseline queries | naive/mix use the same model, questions, prompt and total budget. top_k=12, chunk_top_k=8, entity/relation budgets 2000 each, total context 8000; rerank=false. The official `aquery_llm` saves the answer and the structured evidence of the same call; another retrieval is never passed off as the context of the original answer. |
| Cost and stop protection | 95 LLM and 297 embedding calls; the LLM returned 421,530 input and 115,419 output tokens, 105,856 cached input, reasoning=0; service failures=0, missing usage=0. A cumulative budget of CNY 10, a separate hard deadline, automatic retries off; there are no uncertain requests pending settlement. |

At the [official peak prices](https://www.siliconflow.cn/pricing), LLM input CNY 2/M, output CNY 8/M, cache hits CNY 0.04/M, bge-m3 free. The estimate taking the returned cache volume into account is ¥1.5589; the conservative estimate ignoring all cache discounts is ¥1.7664. ## How US7991757B2 Selects/Ranks Recommendations

US7991757B2 describes a personalization network service that queries multiple external recommenders. In **claim 1**, the system "query the plurality of external recommenders over the computer network for recommendations responsive to the second request, and receive recommendations and associated scores from the external recommenders." Selection is score-based: "an optimization module configured to normalize the associated scores; wherein the recommendations service is further configured to select a subset of the recommendations, based at least in part on the normalized scores."

**Claim 4** adds weighting: "applying weights to each of the recommenders; combining the scores with the weights to produce overall scores; selecting a subset of the recommendations based on the overall scores." **Claim 3** states the optimization module is "further operative to assign weights to the external recommenders."

## How US8095432B1 Selects/Ranks Recommendations

US8095432B1 ranks by social relationship proximity. **Claim 1** recites "ranking, using the processor, the first recommendation with a first rank and the second recommendation with a second rank based on the first relationship proximity and the second relationship proximity, wherein the first rank exceeds the second rank." The list ordering follows rank: "the first recommendation is higher on the recommendation list than the second recommendation based on the first rank exceeding the second rank." Claim 1 also compares interest similarity: "determining that the first member comprises a plurality of interests in common with the inquiring member" and "determining that the first rank is higher than the third rank."

## Interoperation

Neither claim states the two systems interoperate. US7991757B2 claim 1 refers only to "external recommenders" generally, without naming US8095432B1. US8095432B1 claim 1 contains no multi-recommender or external-service element.

**Inference (not stated):** US8095432B1's proximity-ranked engine could conceptually serve as one "external recommender" under US7991757B2's architecture, but no claim wording supports this link.

## How Each Patent Selects or Ranks Recommendations

**US7991757B2** ranks/selects by combining scores from multiple external recommenders. Claim 17 recites: "normalizing scores provided by the recommenders to produce normalized scores; applying weights to each of the recommenders; and combining the normalized scores with the weights to generate overall scores to be used in selecting recommendations." Claim 4 similarly recites "applying weights to each of the recommenders; combining the scores with the weights to produce overall scores; selecting a subset of the recommendations based on the overall scores."

**US8095432B1** ranks by relationship proximity within a social network. Claim 1 recites: "ranking, using the processor, the first recommendation with a first rank and the second recommendation with a second rank based on the first relationship proximity and the second relationship proximity, wherein the first rank exceeds the second rank." The abstract adds that proximity "is closest for friends of the inquiring member, and farthest for strangers."

## Do Either Claims Say the Systems Interoperate?

No. Neither claim references the other patent, its system, or any cross-system interoperability. US7991757B2 claim 17 addresses a "network service to content sites" using registered external recommenders; US8095432B1 claim 1 addresses a "social networking utility" and member relationship proximities. No claim wording in the provided evidence links the two.

## Inference (Not Stated Fact)

Both concern recommendation selection, but on different bases—weighted score aggregation versus social-graph proximity. Any suggestion that one could feed the other is my inference only; the evidence does not support it.

[US9514753B2](https://patents.google.com/patent/US9514753B2/en), Q04 asks which claim contains locality-sensitive hash functions. The real evidence is **Claim 6**: 6. The method of claim 1 , wherein determining the hash values comprises determining the hash values using one or more locality sensitive hash functions.. naive and mix both name claim 6; the same retrieval contains `US9514753B2-chunk-000`, and the file source matches the publication number.

The real complete mix answer

```
**Stated fact (from the patent text):** In US9514753B2, **claim 6** explicitly specifies locality sensitive hash functions. The exact supporting wording is: “wherein determining the hash values comprises determining the hash values using one or more locality sensitive hash functions.”

**Related stated fact:** Claim 7 separately recites hashing “based on a position of the utterance vector with respect to different hyperplanes,” which is distinct from the locality sensitive hash function language in claim 6.

**Inference (not stated in the evidence):** Claim 6 appears to be the claim that most directly ties the claimed hash-value determination to locality sensitive hashing; however, the evidence does not expressly characterize claim 6 as the only such claim or compare it to other claims beyond the quoted text.

### References

- [1] US9514753B2.txt
```

This shows that in this sample, when the original text chunk reaches the context, correct document and claim location is possible. It does not show that the system produces a machine-checkable claim-span evidence object for each statement.

### Failure: graph facts were retrieved, yet a wrong source exclusion was produced

Claim 1 of [US7991757B2](https://patents.google.com/patent/US7991757B2/en) defines a module for registering external recommenders; claim 27 explicitly depends on claim 1 and adds the ability of machine-readable descriptions. Required text:

> **Claim 1:** “a registration module configured to provide functionality for registering an external recommender with a recommendations service”
**Claim 27:** “The system of claim 1 … provide machine readable descriptions of the external recommender.”

The two complete claims lie in different actual chunks: 000 and 001. The technical capabilities were all extracted and merged; the extended-budget Q11 mix call returned the Registration Module record, `file_path=US7991757B2.txt`, `source_id=US7991757B2-chunk-000&lt;SEP&gt;US7991757B2-chunk-001`. But the answer prompt of API 392 keeps the descriptions without these source fields; the target publication number appears only in the user's question and not in the system evidence/reference list. The model calls these registration capabilities **“in a different patent family”** and finally cites [1] US10867122B1.txt.

This source exclusion contradicts the recorded sources. It is not an inference about actual patent-family lineage, nor is a missing technical relation misjudged as an extraction error: **the technical facts were extracted, entered the graph and were retrieved by graph retrieval; the error lies in the chain of source presentation/final attribution.** The omission of the source fields is an observable condition; without a separate source-restoring ablation it cannot be called the only cause of the generation error. The model still did not obtain the original claim text, and the claim-level answer was not completed.

The complete failed answer

```
I do not have enough information to answer this query. The provided **Context** does not contain any document, chunk, or knowledge-graph entity for **US7991757B2**, so I cannot quote Claim 1 or Claim 27 of that patent, nor describe their dependency.

**What is present (explicit evidence):** The context does describe a *registration* capability, but in a different patent family. The knowledge graph states that a "Registration Module" is "configured to provide functionality for registering an external recommender with a recommendations service" and is "configured to allow a provider of an external recommender to provide machine readable descriptions of the external recommender." It also states that "Registration submissions are operative to request registration of recommenders" and are "received from a plurality of recommender providers." However, none of the document chunks in the context contain claim text tied to US7991757B2, and no claim numbers 1 or 27 for that publication appear.

**What is missing:** (1) The text of US7991757B2 Claim 1; (2) the text of Claim 27; (3) any statement of Claim 27's dependency (e.g., "The method of claim 1, further comprising…"). Without these, any description of the added capability or the dependency relationship would be inference rather than evidence, which I will not supply.

**Inference vs. evidence:** It would be an unsupported inference to assume the registration language above belongs to US7991757B2 or that Claim 27 depends from Claim 1. To answer, please provide the claims of US7991757B2 or a document chunk containing them.

### References

- [1] US10867122B1.txt
```

### Another clearly located omission affected by the experimental conditions

[US9218390B2 Claim 2](https://patents.google.com/patent/US9218390B2/en) lies entirely within one chunk. The extraction call API 191 reached this experiment's 3500-token output cap, `finish_reason=length`, and the relation line being written, `Class-Based Language Model Features → GEO_TRI_FIRST`, was not finished. A replay of the actual official parser rejects that line, and the final graph also lacks this explicit membership edge; no other chunk restores it.

**The GEO_TRI_FIRST node and its meaning are kept, and the original text exists completely.** This is a specific extracted relation lost because of this run's output cap; it cannot be called a complete disappearance of the fact, a cross-chunk loss or a proven answer failure. Other items without an explicit edge are not all counted as errors of the same cause, and the baseline index was not modified or rerun with a higher cap to overwrite the original result.

## D. Research judgments

| Question | Conclusion supported by this round's evidence |
| ---|--- |
| Can the current official version provide document-level provenance for patents? | Yes; the file citations of several real answers correspond correctly to the publication numbers; but it is not guaranteed that all graph sources reach the answer context. Supplementary Q11 shows that the structured result keeps the source while the answer still misattributes. “Source data exists” and “the answer binds the source correctly” must therefore be evaluated separately. |
| Can specific claims be traced reliably? | When the required original chunk is retrieved, most questions in this round locate the claim correctly; there is no automatic claim-span guarantee at present. The formatted query output has no explicit claim ID, and internal source spans and external checks cannot be taken as proof of each conclusion of the model. When the text was not retrieved, refusals occurred; it cannot be called generally reliable. |
| Was cross-chunk relation loss reproduced? | Not shown. The dependency chains of the original Q08/Q09 actually lie in one chunk; the genuinely cross-chunk technical relation of US7991757B2 was extracted and merged successfully, keeping both source IDs. The Q11 failure lies in the layer of original-text retrieval/context source and attribution; explicit claim dependencies were not turned into graph structure, and no causal experiment with the same text and a different boundary supports attributing it to chunking. |
| Code defect, design limitation, or conditions of this run? | Q06 is sensitive to the lower top-k/context budget and recovers when it is extended; the truncation omission is caused by this run's 3500 output limit; claim structure and the granularity of graph-source presentation belong to the current system's representation/interface design; the wrong source judgment also involves generation behaviour. No general software defect was confirmed, and the paper's benchmark was not reproduced. |
| Directions worth exploring in depth in a PhD? | Treat claims, dependency constraints and original-text spans as explicit evidence objects; make entity/relation summaries keep their source identity during context construction; combine publication-number constraints with semantic/graph retrieval; measure the retention of facts and sources stage by stage; distinguish safe refusal from wrong attribution when evidence is missing. Incremental consistency was not tested in this round and remains an open question. |

The core `aquery_llm` was actually used; its output contains entities/relationships/chunks/references. `include_references` defaults to false in the core QueryParam and is explicitly true in this round; `include_chunk_content` is a REST parameter, the core result keeps the chunk content directly; `/query/data` corresponds to aquery_data, which generates no final answer but may still call keywords/embedding. The HTTP routes were only checked in the source in this round; no HTTP service was deployed, and no REST test is claimed.

Version limits: Figure 1 of the paper [v3 (2025-04-28)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2410.05779v3) already shows raw chunk IDs, and the current README dates the citations feature to 2025-03; it cannot be claimed that the paper era had no citation mechanism. What is tested here is the 2026 [release v1.5.7](https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/releases/tag/v1.5.7), the specified commercial service and this round's configuration; the behaviour of the new code is not projected back as a conclusion about the paper's original method.

## Reproduction and evidence

Main records: `round2/results/full_Q*_naive.json`, `full_Q*_mix.json`; supplementary results: `supplement_budget_*.json`. Each keeps the original question, the real answer, the entities/relations/chunks/references of the same call, call IDs and times. The index, graph, raw extraction cache, the key-free LLM requests and complete generation responses, and the embedding input/return metadata and persisted index vectors are all kept; the truncated output response was not cached normally by the official code, so the raw record of API 191 is especially important.

Review and location: `full_audit_q01_q05.json`, `full_audit_q06_q11.json`, `supplement_budget_audit.json`, `retrieval_rank_probe.json`, `full_provenance_trace.json`, `extraction_truncation_parser_replay.json`, `actual_chunk_source_mapping.json`. The cost ledger is in `cost_ledger.json`. Role scripts, dependency versions and the original selection list come with the small evidence package.

Method limitations: a purposive sample of 20; single model outputs, and temperature=0 does not guarantee full determinism; no independent double-blind human annotation; the baseline budget is below the source defaults; additional gleaning=0, rerank off; the sensitivity check changes several budget parameters at once; incremental insertion not tested. Successes, incomplete answers and source errors of all modes are kept; no winner is picked by preference.
